body:
**Adversarial review, round 1** on `3a4d064` by claude-opus-5-5 (builder: claude-sonnet-5-5).

Approve, with one low finding and nothing blocking. App code: both `/latest` and `/history` now look up sensors with `find` (`Object.hasOwn`), so FR-007 is applied wherever a sensor is looked up; no other sensor lookup exists. Percent-encoded IDs such as `%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` also stay safe, because WHATWG URL doesn't decode the pathname, so they never match a real key. The history handler matches FR-001 to FR-005: bounds are inclusive (`>=`/`<=`), the check is `to - from > 7d` (strictly greater), unknown sensors get a 404 with `unknown_sensor`, an empty range gives a 200 with `[]`, and readings come back oldest first because `data.ts` is already in time order. `app/openapi.yaml` documents `/history` with the `History` schema and the 400 and 404 responses (FR-006), so the contract matches. The prototype-ID tests are real: without the `hasOwn` guard, `toString`, `constructor` and `__proto__` would all have returned 200 on `/latest` and `/history`, so the tests would fail. Workflow and tooling: `epic.yml` passes its inputs through env rather than interpolating them into `run`, and `epic-pr.ts` reads the lead from the locked spec tag and checks it against `triggering_actor`. The `Spec:` re-point in `open-pr.ts` uses the same pattern as `trace.ts` and only runs in build mode with the revision the workflow authorized. `do_not_enforce_on_create` is needed so the API can create the `epic/` branch; the PR and review rules still apply.

- **F-1** [low] `land` lists merged sync PRs as milestones — `lanes/epic-pr.ts:34`
  The `land` op takes every merged PR whose base is `epic/<id>` and puts them all under '## Milestones'. The `sync` op in the same file also opens PRs into `epic/<id>` (sync/<id>-rN → epic/<id>). Once one of those is merged, it shows up in the epic PR body as a milestone. Their bodies have no provenance blocks, so the provenance table is unaffected, but the milestone list is wrong. Filtering on the builder's head-branch prefix, or on `Closes #<milestone issue>` matched against `spec.milestones`, would fix it. Related: the list makes a single request with `per_page=100` and no pagination, so an epic with more than 100 closed PRs into its branch would be cut short without any warning.


Only @dharishan04 can close a finding without a fix: `/dismiss <F-n> <reason>`.
